evidence.title: DEVIATION: testing.json wiring does not actually pass -tags=integration
evidence.description: The plan's §11 checklist requires `.vrooli/testing.json` to make `vrooli scenario test vrooli-emulator` invoke `go test -tags=integration`. The change adds a `phases.integration` block (enabled=true, timeout=5m), but the schema at scenarios/test-genie/schemas/testing.schema.json defines `phases.<name>` with only generic phase_options (no build_tags field). So the runner does NOT receive `-tags=integration`. The runbook explicitly acknowledges this: 'vrooli scenario test vrooli-emulator does not currently pass -tags=integration to go test; until the runner gains build-tag support, run the command above directly.' This means plan checklist item 11.10 (vrooli scenario test vrooli-emulator exits 0 end-to-end exercising the new suite) cannot be met without a runner-level change that is out of scope for this item.

improvement_suggestions.description: Add a follow-up execute item to extend the testing-runner schema with `phases.integration.build_tags` (or equivalent) and have the runner pass it through to `go test`. Without this, `vrooli scenario test vrooli-emulator` silently skips the integration suite even though Phase 1 ostensibly delivered runner wiring. Until then, the runbook is the only path to executing the suite.

When `r2-i1` is filed/executed (wire WithCaptures() in api/main.go), add a thin integration assertion that hits the real running scenario binary and confirms screenshots are persisted — today only the test harness exercises the captures path.

Phase 2 owns first WebSocket coverage (per r2-d2=A). When that lands, add a GCT-visible scenario health check that exercises POST /sessions + WS upgrade end-to-end so future review rounds get WS coverage automatically.

Fix the dead $schema reference in .vrooli/testing.json (currently `../../../../scripts/scenarios/testing/schemas/testing.schema.json`; actual path is `scenarios/test-genie/schemas/testing.schema.json`). Pre-existing, not introduced by this item, but cheap to clean up.
